claims.text: The Australian Institute of Quantity Surveyors (AIQS) — described on its own site as "the peak professional standards body for built environment cost professionals" — accredits undergraduate and postgraduate university quantity surveying and construction economics programs in Australia and internationally. AIQS states this accreditation process "ensures the programs meet and uphold educational standards relevant to quantity surveying and construction management" and "externally verifies the program's quality," with graduates of accredited programs recognised by AIQS as meeting the academic requirements for entry to the profession and for pathways to AIQS Membership or a Migration Skills Assessment. AIQS also administers the Certified Quantity Surveyor (CQS) professional designation, attained at Member, Fellow, or Life Fellow grade, gated by an Assessment of Professional Competence (a mapped Professional Work Experience Diary) plus a minimum of three years' demonstrated professional experience and a clean AIQS Code of Conduct record for the preceding five years.

claims.scope: Covers only the quantity-surveying side of the combined O*NET occupation 11-9021 and only AIQS's professional accreditation/certification standards — a peak-body instrument, not government licensing. It does not cover the construction-management side, which is regulated separately and unevenly by state building-practitioner licensing regimes (e.g. Victorian Building Authority, Queensland Building and Construction Commission, NSW Fair Trading) rather than by AIQS. Does not establish that AIQS accreditation or CQS certification is legally mandatory to practise as a quantity surveyor in Australia (unlike a licence) — it is a voluntary professional-standards and credentialing scheme.
